# Cortiblex (cortisolan acetate) — Prescribing Information

*Fictional drug. Synthetic prescribing information written for this tutorial only.*

## Approved Indications

Cortiblex is approved for:

1. Short-course treatment (up to 14 days) of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid
   arthritis flare in adults.
2. Adjunct therapy for acute severe allergic reactions, in combination with
   standard emergency treatment.

## Contraindications

- Active systemic fungal infection.
- Administration of a live or live-attenuated vaccine within the prior 4 weeks.

## Adverse Reactions

Common (≥5% of patients): insomnia, increased appetite, fluid retention, mood
changes.

Serious, requiring immediate escalation: adrenal insufficiency (fatigue, low
blood pressure, nausea after stopping), gastrointestinal bleeding (black
stools, severe abdominal pain), severe mood changes (mania, psychosis), vision
changes (blurred vision, eye pain).

## Dosing

Adults: 40 mg once daily for the flare's duration, tapered rather than stopped
abruptly if used for more than 5 days.
